prompts.turn:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: animation cel atlas for an existing original navy-haired male in dark purple armor.
Image 1 is the approved character identity, proportion, armor and ink/color reference. Image 2 is ONLY a rough 3D turn-and-exit staging reference, do not copy its low-detail rendering.
Create ONE transparent RGBA sprite sheet, exactly 4 columns x 3 rows, 12 separate evenly spaced full-body cels, NO text, NO borders, NO floor, NO shadows. Prefer 2048 x 2048. Each cel has generous transparent margins and the SAME character height, same foot baseline and pelvis location within its cell, camera at standing eye level.
Read left-to-right top-to-bottom. Row 1 is a planted turn AWAY from the viewer: cel 1 same left-facing stance as image1; cel 2 left rear three-quarter with a small planted pivot step; cel 3 clear BACK view with both shoulders and back of head visible; cel 4 right-facing rear three-quarter stance, ready to walk toward screen RIGHT and slightly into depth.
Rows 2 and 3 are ONE natural 8-phase WALK cycle in this SAME right-facing rear-three-quarter view: right heel forward contact, down/recoil, passing with left knee forward, up, left heel forward contact, down/recoil, passing with right knee forward, up. The near and far legs actually exchange positions every half cycle. Natural upright hips, gently bent knees, restrained coordinated arm swing; head and chest keep their volume and identical proportions.
Keep navy layered swept-back hair, pale skin, charcoal undersuit, lean human thighs of normal thickness, purple segmented armor, narrow gauntlets and boots, original asymmetrical shoulder/cuff design; preserve anatomical left and right through turn, do NOT mirror hardware to the opposite arm. The broken chain cuff stays on the same anatomical wrist, no extended chain or weapon. No smiling, no exaggerated expression, no new costume, no white background. Sharp clean hand-drawn cel shading, matching original illustration. All whole bodies fit inside their own equal cells. No stretching between drawings, no noodles, no backwards knees.

prompts.opposite_passing:
Use case: sketch-to-render, animation pose correction. Return a TWO-CEL transparent sheet side-by-side.
Image1 defines the exact character, rear-three-quarter viewpoint, drawing and clothes. Image2 is the TWO-POSE LEG GUIDE that overrides the repeated leg poses in image1. Copy image2's upper body and turn each colored leg guide into the SAME character's charcoal trouser legs and purple armored boots. Remove all diagram colors; no background.
CRITICAL DEPTH ID: cyan is the NEAR leg, orange is the FAR leg. The NEAR thigh belongs to the right side of the image's hip and must be rendered IN FRONT at intersections. Do not swap the two at the hip.
Cel A (left): NEAR thigh crosses diagonally forward to the RIGHT, near knee then near foot lead on screen-right; FAR leg trails back to the LEFT behind that thigh. This is opposite the repeated contact pose in image1.
Cel B (right): NEAR leg is straight and load bearing, an unbroken vertical contour from near hip down to the planted boot. FAR thigh and knee lift toward screen RIGHT BEHIND the standing near thigh, far heel folds back behind the standing calf. Do not put the raised thigh in front. The single vertical NEAR thigh must visibly OCCLUDE part of the bent far leg.
Natural leg thickness, human knee bend, original boot shape, same head/body height in both cels, matching face/hair/armor. No new weapon. Keep upper body silhouette and torso proportions. Both characters fit fully with margins. Clean professional cel shading, no labels.
